questions.questionText: What is the main difference between let and const in JavaScript/TypeScript?

const only works with primitive types
const variables cannot be reassigned after declaration

options.text: Enforces strict runtime type coercion
Restricts the variable to primitive values only
Represents a function return type of null

"boolean"
"object"

questions.questionText: How does the JavaScript Event Loop handle microtasks compared to macrotasks?

options.text: Macrotasks always execute ahead of microtasks regardless of queue state
Microtasks run on a separate background thread in parallel
Microtasks (e.g., Promise callbacks) are executed immediately after the current synchronous script and before the next macrotask
Microtasks and macrotasks are interleaved alternately in a round-robin schedule

questions.explanation: All pending jobs in the microtask queue run to exhaustion after the current synchronous frame and before picking the next task from the macrotask queue.

questions.questionText: In TypeScript, what is the key difference between an interface and a type alias for object models?

options.text: Interfaces do not support generic parameters
Type aliases cannot describe function signatures
Interfaces can be declaration-merged by defining them multiple times, whereas type aliases cannot
Type aliases cannot model union or intersection types

questions.explanation: Multiple interface declarations with the same identifier in the same scope merge their property definitions.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of the "unknown" type in TypeScript compared to "any"?

options.text: unknown allows arbitrary property access without checks
unknown is only allowed as a return type for async functions
unknown is type-safe: you must narrow its type with checks before calling methods or accessing properties
unknown is an alias for undefined

questions.explanation: unknown represents any value but requires runtime type narrowing or type assertions before performing operations.

questions.questionText: What occurs when a JavaScript closure is created?

options.text: The function is converted into an anonymous asynchronous worker
An inner function retains access to its enclosing lexical scope even after the outer function has executed
Memory is immediately reclaimed by the garbage collector
Global scope variables are copied into a frozen record

questions.explanation: A closure combines a function with references to its surrounding lexical environment.

questions.questionText: Which TypeScript utility type constructs a type with all properties of T set to optional?

options.text: Required<T>
Partial<T>
Readonly<T>
Omit<T, K>

questions.explanation: Partial<T> transforms all declared properties of T into optional properties.

questions.questionText: In TypeScript, what is a distributive conditional type and when does distribution happen?

options.text: When a mapped type uses the -readonly modifier
When a generic conditional type T extends U ? X : Y operates on a naked type parameter T that is instantiated with a union
When an interface inherits from multiple parent interfaces simultaneously
When a function overloads more than five signature variants

questions.explanation: Conditional types distribute over union members automatically when the checked type parameter is bare (not wrapped in a tuple or object).

questions.questionText: How does V8 optimize JavaScript object property lookups at runtime?

options.text: By compiling every object declaration into a C++ struct at interpretation time
Using Hidden Classes (Shapes) and Inline Caches (ICs) to bypass hash table dictionary lookups
By converting all property names into sequential 32-bit integer indexes
By storing all objects in a flat global array

questions.explanation: V8 assigns hidden classes based on property addition order and uses inline caching at call sites to avoid dictionary lookups.

questions.questionText: What technique ensures complete type narrowing for discriminated union types in TypeScript (exhaustiveness checking)?

options.text: Using the Object.freeze() method on all union instances
Casting the default branch to "any"
Throwing a generic runtime TypeError without type annotations
Assigning the remaining value in the default switch branch to a variable typed as "never"

questions.explanation: Assigning to type "never" produces a compile-time error if any union variant was unhandled in the conditional branches.

questions.questionText: What is the memory impact of WeakMap and WeakSet in long-running Node.js processes?

options.text: Keys in WeakMap are held weakly, permitting garbage collection when no other references exist
WeakMap stores primitive values in the C++ stack rather than V8 heap
WeakMap causes circular reference memory leaks in V8 heaps
WeakMap keys persist in memory indefinitely until clear() is invoked

questions.explanation: WeakMap references to object keys are weak, allowing garbage collection when keys are otherwise unreferenced.

questions.questionText: How do JavaScript Symbol.asyncIterator and AsyncGenerators coordinate backpressure?

options.text: By buffering chunks in an OS-level TCP socket
By throwing a QuotaExceededError when consumer falls behind
By blocking the Node.js event loop synchronously until read
Each call to .next() returns a Promise that only resolves when the generator yields, letting consumers pace production

questions.explanation: Async generators yield promises for each iterator step, allowing consumers to await each step before requesting the next.
